title: Supermassive Black Hole Seed Formation
bottleneck: Billion-solar-mass black holes exist by redshift 7, less than a gigayear after the Big Bang, but no seed mechanism (direct collapse, Pop III remnants, dense-cluster runaways) is confirmed, and growth-rate requirements strain Eddington-limited accretion. JWST's 'little red dots' may be over-massive black holes deepening the puzzle. Sustained super-Eddington accretion could grow light seeds fast enough, but it requires special conditions that may not be generic.
why_it_blocks: Black hole seeds are the missing first chapter of galaxy formation, and their origin constrains early-universe physics.
current_state: All seed channels remain viable; LISA's future detections of high-z mergers could discriminate between light and heavy seeds. JWST's discovery of abundant faint active nuclei at high redshift is reshaping seed and growth models in real time.
